advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document how `_resolve_target` handles a provider-qualified `model` combined with an explicit `provider` (honor, error on conflict, or explicitly ignore) rather than silently dropping the provider.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:158 `return model` — the explicit `provider` argument is never consulted on this branch
`resolve_class` passes `slot.provider` into `_resolve_target` (line 169) but it is discarded when the model is already qualified
No test covers a slot supplying BOTH a qualified `model` and a conflicting `provider`; `test_an_already_qualified_model_is_not_double_prefixed` only exercises a qualified model with no provider
advisory.finding: `_resolve_target` returns a provider-qualified `model` as-is when it contains ':', silently ignoring an explicitly-configured `provider` on the same slot/entry. A config with `model: "openai:gpt-4o"` and `provider: "bedrock"` resolves to `openai:gpt-4o`, dropping the operator's explicit provider with no error.
scenarios: An operator sets a `provider:model` id and also an explicit `provider` (e.g. via env `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER`) expecting the provider to win

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make empty-`model` handling consistent between slots and fallback entries (either both default or both raise), and add a test pinning the chosen behavior for a slot.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:76-78 `model = raw.get("model")` / `if not model:` / `raise LLMConfigError("a fallback entry requires a non-empty 'model'")` — the entry path rejects empty model
No test asserts behavior for a slot with an explicitly empty `model` string
advisory.finding: A slot with an explicitly empty `model` (e.g. `{"model": ""}`) silently resolves to the built-in per-class default because `raw.get("model") or _DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]` treats `""` as unset, whereas a fallback entry with an empty `model` raises `LLMConfigError`. The same empty-model input is a typed error in one path and a silent default in the other.
scenarios: An operator typos `model = ""` on a class slot and is silently routed to the default model instead of getting a config error

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting parse_class_slots raises LLMConfigError for an unknown top-level class name (e.g. {"bogus": {"model": "m"}}).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:148-150: `unknown = sorted(set(table) - set(CLASS_NAMES)) ... raise LLMConfigError(f"unknown model-class name(s): ...")`
test at line 210 calls `mc.resolve_class("fronteir", slots)` — exercises resolve_class guard (model_classes.py:166-167), not parse_class_slots's unknown-key branch
ABSENCE: no test calls `parse_class_slots({"bogus": {...}})` expecting LLMConfigError
src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:76-78: `model = raw.get("model") ... if not model: raise LLMConfigError("a fallback entry requires a non-empty 'model'")`
ABSENCE: fallback tests (lines 109-182) all pass entries carrying a model; none omit it
src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:176-177: `if name not in CLASS_NAMES: raise LLMConfigError(f"unknown model class: {name!r} ...")`
ABSENCE: resolve_fallback_chain is only called with valid class names (line 173); no test asserts it raises for an unknown class
advisory.finding: parse_class_slots's unknown-class-NAME rejection branch is untested. The docstring and commit both name 'an unknown class name' as a typed error, and the code raises LLMConfigError at lines 148-150, but every test passes only valid class names to parse_class_slots; the sole unknown-class test (test_an_unknown_class_name_is_a_typed_error_not_a_silent_default) exercises resolve_class's separate guard (lines 166-167), not this branch. A regression that let parse_class_slots silently ignore an unknown top-level key would pass all tests.
merged_from: The 'a fallback entry requires a non-empty model' error branch is untested. _parse_fallback_entry raises LLMConfigError when model is falsy (model_classes.py:76-78), but no test supplies a fallback entry lacking a model key.

resolve_fallback_chain's unknown-class guard (model_classes.py:176-177) is entirely untested. resolve_class's identical guard is covered, but resolve_fallback_chain is a distinct public function whose LLMConfigError path has no test.
scenarios: A refactor removes/weakens the `set(table) - set(CLASS_NAMES)` check; a typo'd config class key is silently dropped and the pass runs on the default model — the exact silent-misroute failure this epic exists to remove.
